verdicts.trueWording: I generally like to give an NPC one distinguishing characteristic
verdicts.note: Raw PDF (Wayback capture of wizards.com DM_Experience_2011.pdf) extracted with pdftotext. Sentence ends 'before moving on', in the column headed 'The Dungeon Master Experience: T’wit', December 2011 | DUNGEON 197, in the run of paragraphs beginning 'I keep my NPC descriptions brief as well.' Quote appears word for word; both limbs (one characteristic, then move on) supported.

verdicts.trueWording: I don’t frontload information. I let it trickle out
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, T’wit column, the paragraph immediately after the NPC-description paragraph. Continues 'in dribs and drabs' and explains he controls the pace. Quote verbatim (curly apostrophe); both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: I pepper them with local rumors—some true, some false
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, column 'The Dungeon Master Experience: Lies My DM Told Me', December 2011 | DUNGEON 197. Sentence opens 'Whenever the characters arrive in a new village, town, or city'. Quote verbatim; village/town/city and true-and-false limbs both supported.

verdicts.trueWording: When in doubt, tell the players things that are true.
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, 'Lies My DM Told Me', under the subhead 'Lessons Learned'. Quote verbatim as a standalone sentence; the next sentence supports the second limb, saying even the old D&D adventures tended to carry more true rumors than false ones.

verdicts.trueWording: names that sound human but seem grounded in a
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, column 'The Dungeon Master Experience: What’s in a Name?', December 2011 | DUNGEON 197, in the paragraph on human names. The sentence begins 'The trick is coming up with' and closes on a world of fantasy rather than reality. Quote verbatim; every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Never force yourself to create more than you must.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF textual.ru/rpg/dungeoncraft.pdf (John H. Kim’s preservation of the 29-part Dragon series, bylined Ray Winninger on its title page), chapter 2 'World Building, Part I — From Dragon Magazine 256'. Printed under the display head 'First Rule of Dungeoncraft:', so the rule’s name and text both match. The source field’s parenthetical about a later WotC role is biographical and is not carried by this page.

verdicts.trueWording: a Master of the Docks who authorizes all cargo
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, chapter 3 'World Building, Part II — From Dragon Magazine 257', under 'Home Base', in the 'City' home-base template. The passage says bureaucrats governing the city are dedicated to trade and knowledge functions, giving this office and a Dean of Colleges as examples; the sentence continues 'that comes in and out of the city'. Quote verbatim; every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: a place where adventurers gather to swap boasts, rumors, and legends
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, chapter 7 'The Rumor Mill and Maps — From Dragon Magazine 261', section 'The Rumor Mill'. The instruction is to plan a fairly obvious rumor mill in your base of operations (the home base of the preceding chapters), which carries the claim’s 'home settlement'. Quote verbatim; every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: better to develop two really good ideas than four
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, Dragon 261 chapter, section 'Interesting NPCs'. The floor is phrased 'you should try to create at least two such personalities' for the base of operations, which supports the claim’s minimum of two interesting NPCs; the quoted sentence continues 'or five mediocre ideas' (claim says 'ones'). Quote verbatim; both limbs supported, the floor in slightly softer words than 'sets'.

verdicts.trueWording: does not make any reference to the viewer
verdicts.note: Raw PDF paizo.com/writersguidelines/dungeon_writer_guidelines.pdf, section 'Read-Aloud Text (Mandatory)'. Full sentence says read-aloud text gives a bare-bones description of the encounter area and then the quoted clause. Quote verbatim; limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Avoid phrases such as “you see,” “as you enter the room,”
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, 'Read-Aloud Text (Mandatory)'. Quote verbatim including the curly quotation marks; the rationale limb is carried by the rest of the sentence, which bars other phrases that assume any action whatsoever on behalf of the players.

verdicts.trueWording: should only rarely run more than a few sentences
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, 'Read-Aloud Text (Mandatory)', penultimate sentence of the section: read-aloud text for an encounter is what carries the cap. Quote verbatim; limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Long sections of read-aloud text are better served as player handouts
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, 'Read-Aloud Text (Mandatory)', final sentence of the section, immediately after the few-sentences cap. Quote verbatim; limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: avoid including descriptions of any creatures in the room
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, 'Read-Aloud Text (Mandatory)'. Quote verbatim inside the sentence beginning 'You should also'; the rationale limb is supported by its 'since' clause, which says creatures’ activities and positions in the room often depend on multiple factors (whether they hear the PCs coming, night or day, and so on).

verdicts.trueWording: The editors greatly dislike printing the words “This room is empty”
verdicts.note: Same raw PDF, section 'The Adventure’s Encounters (Mandatory)', closing the paragraph on encounter sections: if you have nothing to say for any category the area is not an encounter. The sentence ends 'in DUNGEON', which is the magazine, supporting that limb. Quote verbatim.
